newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues detailed rules on insurance.
newsitem.headline: China issues detailed rules on insurance.

text.p: China's central bank has published new detailed rules on the insurance industry to complement an insurance law passed in 1995, officials and state media said on Friday.
"These are detailed rules designed to enrich the Insurance Law. most (of the) contents were not included in the previous law," an official of the People's Bank of China said.
China's Insurance Law took effect on October 1, 1995.

The new rules specify regulations for setting up insurance companies and clearly define the business scope of various types of insurers, the Financial News said. The minimum registered capital of a nationwide insurance company is 500 million yuan and the requirement for a regional insurer is 200 million yuan.
The new rules took effect from July 25 this year.
The rules stipulate that insurance capital must be deposited in banks, invested in treasury bonds or used in line with rules set by the State Council, or cabinet, the newspaper said.
The new rules also regulate the business conduct of insurance companies and specify requirements for insurance premium rates.
They also stipulate punishments for violations, with firms facing a maximum fine of 500,000 yuan for illegal conduct.
